title: TokFlow comm-slimming and prefill-hedge scheduler for multi-GPU runtime
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Problem: In heterogeneous multi-GPU runs we observe tail latency spikes and elevated token costs under mixed prefill+decode workloads. Root causes include conservative NCCL synchronization during KV/cache handoffs, suboptimal attention kernel selection for short vs long sequence phases, and lack of a coordinated hedging/fallback policy when a device experiences slow prefill. Goal: implement a scheduler (TokFlow) that coordinates tensor/pipeline parallel transfers and kernel hints to maximize NCCL overlap while bounding tail latency and preserving throughput. Approach: 1) Comm-slimming: introduce lightweight comm-sparsification for KV-cache exchanges during prefill by only exchanging hot KV stripes (top-k by activation magnitude heuristic) then backfilling asynchronously. This reduces all-reduce volume and enables increased NCCL overlap with compute. 2) Phase-aware kernel selection: use an online phase detector (prefill vs steady decode vs long-context fill) to bias kernel choices (fused-attention vs tiled-attention kernels) and recompute kernel hints at rendezvous points. 3) Prefill-hedge scheduler: when token prefill latency for a rank exceeds an adaptive threshold, trigger hedging: spawn a redundant decode on a compatible spare device or route to a lower-cost but faster quantized variant. Hedging decisions are cost-aware and respect SLA budgets. 4) Rendezvous windows: align microbatch boundaries into rendezvous windows permitting NCCL streams to overlap with neighboring stage compute; schedule NCCL via exclusive stream priorities and opportunistic comm-windows to reduce blocking. 5) Observability and rollback: add per-token latency tagging, NCCL overlap ratio, and kernel selection histograms to the Console and benchmark dashboards. Deliverables: - Runtime scheduler code with toggles behind feature flag and config knobs for top-k stripe size, hedge thresholds, and kernel hint expiry. - Design doc + microbench harness. - Benchmarks: latency P50/P95/P99 and cost-per-token on representative LLMs (7B, 13B, 70B) across homogeneous and heterogeneous GPU clusters. Links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/TokFlow+Comm-Slimming+Design , PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892 , benchmark dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/runtime/tokflow-experiments
acceptance_criteria: Feature flag exists and can enable TokFlow scheduling end-to-end
P95 latency improves or P99 does not regress by >10% compared to baseline in at least two of three benchmark configs
Tokenized cost-per-1M-tokens decreases by >=5% on mixed prefill+decode workloads in at least one heterogeneous cluster config
Kernel selection changes are visible in the Console and per-route kernel histograms are emitted
Hedge triggers are rate-limited and recorded; no cascading redundant spawn storms observed during stress test
notes: Design leans on model-agnostic KV stripe heuristic; we may need model-specific tuning for very sparse attention models (sparse transformers). Budget for two spike days to iterate on stripe sizing and hedge thresholds.
